metadata.note: Skill teardown of skills/make/guests/SKILL.md (SOURCE-SNAPSHOT SHA-256 dc9db967…; supervisor's episode.source_sha256 d38fbfba…). `guests` is the sibling of `fellows` — the same Claude-branded bookends and the same 'the recording plays as is' contract, but ONE structural difference: no feedback beat, no Professor Bear's notes, GATE G (guest approves the framing) in place of GATE N. Teaches: the six-beat spine (COLD OPEN · SUMMARY · THE GUEST'S VIDEO · RECAP · YOUR TURN · HAI OUTRO), the absence-not-toggle design that prevents an org-chart inversion (a fellow is mentored; a board member is not evaluated by staff), GATE G as a third-party gate (SKIPPED under --silent, never auto-passed), the screen-clean carve-out for the source recording, and privacy-aware naming (first names by default, standing named when the guest is a board member). No guest recording is transcoded or shipped — this teardown is source-backed per SELF-DEMO LAW's feasibility fallback (running a real guests episode would require a guest's video and the guest's actual signature on a review file via GATE G). Kokoro am_onyx throughout — free, local. No captions. Outro is ClaudeTitleOutro (OUTRO-LOCK.md locks @NikBearBrown handle) because this is a claude-liam TEARDOWN; the guests skill it explains uses the standard HAI outro, and that channel-follows-outro rule is the falsifiability beat itself. Portrait companion — native 9:16 layouts (not a center-crop of the landscape master). channel_title metadata deliberately omitted — its compile-overlay bleeds past portrait safe.b (feedback_channel_title_portrait_bleed). Three SkillTeardown*916 wrappers plus the BrutalistHesitantWriter portrait-aware scale patch are copies of the fellows episode's scene-source (credited in SOURCES.md), registered in this isolated toolkit's Root.tsx for this run.

beats.role_note: The pipeline — the required beat spine. Six beats, not nine. Input: guest's raw recording. Output: a wrapped reel + a signed REVIEW.md.
beats.narration_text: The spine is fixed. Six beats. Not nine. The composer cold open names the guest's standing and the video's subject — never a progress report. A summary beat written from the faster-whisper transcript. Then the guest's video plays as is — that is beat three. A recap, descriptive only, no evaluation. A Your Turn prompt. And the standard Humanitarians AI outro. Same shape every episode. Only the middle is the guest's own material.

beats.role_note: VERDICT — artifact card. Recapitulates the skill in six lines.
beats.narration_text: The verdict. Guests is a frame around a guest's own recording — nothing more, nothing less. Six beats, not nine. Professor Bear's notes are absent by design — a board member is not evaluated by staff. GATE G moves the signature from Bear to the guest, and dash-dash silent will queue the reel, never auto-pass it. Screen-clean cleans the recording, but the talk itself is never trimmed to fit a runtime. The narrator voice belongs to the channel, not the guest. And the outro is the standard HAI outro — because the channel is HAI.

artifactLines: guests wraps a guest's own recording — the talk itself plays untouched.
SIX beats, not nine: cold open · summary · THE VIDEO · recap · Your Turn · HAI outro.
NO feedback beat, absent by design — a board member is not evaluated by staff.
GATE G: the GUEST signs the summary and recap; --silent queues, never auto-passes.
screen-clean cleans the source; NEVER cut or excerpt the talk to fit a runtime.
One persistent narrator per channel; the outro is HAI's — the channel picks it.
